author: Associated Press
description:
While officials say proposed revisions will encourage more enrollment, advocates say it will undermine the program

The Trump administration has said it plans to overhaul Head Start, tossing out many of the regulations that are the hallmark of the early education program for the nation’s neediest children.

Officials from the Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the federally funded preschool program, said on Thursday the proposed changes would encourage more local decision-making, but the proposal has sparked alarm across the Head Start community, where advocates say it threatens the backbone of the antipoverty initiative.

Continue reading...
title: Trump administration announces changes to Head Start in overhaul

author: Associated Press
description:
Settlement ends years-long legal battle over collapse of 18-story hotel that was under construction in New Orleans

A judge approved a $106m settlement on Thursday that ends a years-long legal battle over the deadly 2019 collapse of a Hard Rock Hotel that was under construction in New Orleans.

The 18-story hotel project partially collapsed in October 2019 , killing three people and damaging nearby property. A grand jury ultimately decided against indicting anyone in the deadly collapse, but lawsuits were filed, including one brought by the city of New Orleans in August 2020 naming the building owners, their partners and contractors.

Continue reading...
title: Judge approves $106m settlement over deadly 2019 Hard Rock Hotel collapse

author: Alexandra Villarreal in New York
description:
Expansion of immigration enforcement at US airports puts employees at odds with agents seeking 2,000 daily arrests

A dramatic increase in immigration enforcement at US airports has reportedly placed the airline industry at odds with the Trump administration as workers decline to help federal officials arrest their targets – many of whom have pending applications for visas, asylum or green cards.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) – both part of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) – have expanded their collaboration to make as many as three dozen daily arrests at US airports last month, the
title: Airline workers reportedly decline to help US agents as Trump migrant crackdown accelerates

author: Johana Bhuiyan
description:
Shift in monitoring methods has led to revenue boost for Geo Group, a private prison firm, that also makes the device

The US is tracking nearly 54,000 immigrants through GPS-enabled ankle monitors as part of a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) electronic surveillance program, according to private prison corporation The Geo Group. Early last year, just 17,000 immigrants were wearing the devices..

The Geo Group owns BI Inc, the company that runs ICE’s intensive supervision appearance program (ISAP), and reported the numbers in its earnings call on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: ICE is now tracking nearly 54,000 immigrants via ankle monitors

Marles maintains gambling reforms about striking a ‘balance’ over ‘complex’ issue

Richard Marles, the deputy prime minister, said the government still intends to get its gambling reforms past parliament despite opposition from the Greens and the Coalition, who both argue that they do not go far enough.

I mean, we are doing more in terms of breaking the link between gambling advertising and sport, more in terms of protecting our kids from being exposed to gambling advertising on TV and radio at the times when they would be watching and listening. We’re doing more in terms of supporting BetStop, which helps people who identify to restrict their own gambling habits.

So this is really important legislation and we’ll work with the parties across the parliament to get it passed.

It’s also an area where you need to str
title: Australia news live: Surge in EV demand and fuel diplomacy push send trade surplus to nine-year low

author: Robert Mackey and Guardian staff
description:
Executive orders come after supreme court rejected president’s first bid to restrict guarantee enshrined in US constitution

Donald Trump on Thursday signed two executive orders that the White House said aims to restrict eligibility for birthright citizenship and ban “birth tourism”.

The ‌orders come just over a month after the United States supreme court rejected Trump’s first attempt to restrict the guarantee of birthright citizenship enshrined in the US constitution.

Continue reading...
title: Trump signs new orders targeting birthright citizenship

description:
Westminster council has recommended banning ‘vertical drinking’ or ordering at the bar in new draft licensing policy

No 10 has vowed to confiscate powers from local councils which try to restrict customers from standing up while drinking in pubs or ordering at the bar.

It comes after the Guardian revealed on Thursday that Westminster council in central London recommended not allowing “vertical drinking” or ordering at the bar in its new draft licensing policy.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It is British life’: No 10 vows to stop councils trying to limit standing in pubs

description:
Republican senator, 84, was taken to hospital after fall in June and has been absent from Senate since

  • US politics live – latest updates

The Republican US senator Mitch McConnell has been discharged from a rehabilitation center following the fall that left him hospitalized, he announced on Thursday.

McConnell, 84, whose weeks‑long absence from Capitol Hill fueled mounting speculation about his health, said he will continue his recovery at home.

Continue reading...
title: Mitch McConnell leaves rehab center to continue recovery from fall at home

author: Richard Adams Education editor
description:
Exclusive: Academics say university must take responsibility for ‘grotesque racism’ unleashed and hold independent inquiry

The University of Cambridge’s leaders deserve blame for the “grotesque racism unleashed” by Jason Arday’s appointment as professor, according to academics calling for the university to hold an independent inquiry.

The Guardian understands that senior dons at Cambridge are circulating a joint letter calling for an inquiry into the processes and circumstances around Arday being given the position, with many suggesting the university wanted a “quick fix” to improve the diversity of its staff.

Continue reading...
title: Cambridge dons demand accountability over Jason Arday appointment

author: Jeremy Barr in Washington
description:
The 2-1 vote along party lines repealed ‘national cap’ that served as a key check on consolidation of the TV industry

In a historic vote on Thursday morning, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) voted along party lines to overturn a key check against the consolidation of the television industry, throwing out a rule that prevented any one company from owning stations that collectively reach more than 39% of all US TV households.

The vote is a win for television conglomerates that aim to expand their reach across the country, particularly conservative-leaning companies like Sinclair Broadcast Group and Nexstar.

Continue reading...
title: FCC overturns limit on local TV ownership in win for media conglomerates

author: Raphael Boyd
description:
Emma Atkinson, 38, was seven months pregnant when she fell from window of flat in Leeds tower block

A pregnant woman who died from a nine-storey fall had her baby safely delivered 30 minutes after her death, an inquest has heard.

Emma Atkinson, 38, was seven months pregnant when she fell from the window of her father’s flat in Shakespeare Towers in the Burmantofts area of Leeds, on 22 October 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Baby safely delivered after mother died in nine-storey fall

author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Ben Quinn; produced by Bryony Moore and Leonore Schick; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin
description:
Joshua Bonehill-Paine, a former neo-Nazi activist, has been offered a role as an adviser to the Conservative party by Kemi Badenoch after he withdrew as a Tory candidate for next year’s local elections. The role will reportedly be focused on how young men become radicalised.

Bonehill-Paine was convicted of harassing a Jewish MP and has previously described himself as a ‘nationalist, fascist, theorist and supporter of white rights’. He says he has carried out counter-extremism work since he was released from prison.

Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian political correspondent Ben Quinn – watch on YouTube

Continue reading...
title: Why has Kemi Badenoch given a former neo-Nazi an advisory role? – The Latest

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Passengers awaiting Northern and TransPennine trains advised not to travel, with cancellations and other services delayed

Trains across parts of north-west England have ground to a halt after a power failure hit the signalling centre controlling the railway in the region.

Passengers awaiting Northern and TransPennine trains have been advised not to travel, with widespread cancellations and other services delayed by more than an hour already.

Continue reading...
title: Trains stop across north-west England after power cut hits signalling centre

author: Petra Stock
description:
As Australia prepares for the H5 bird flu to potentially rip through hundreds of species, residents of the Limestone Coast are already seeing the impacts

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

It’s only been three weeks since H5 bird flu was detected on South Australia’s Limestone Coast, and already encounters with sick or dead birds are becoming commonplace.

Maureen Christie, who lives in the seaside town of Carpenter Rocks, has been observing and protecting birds in the region for decades. She is now witnessing many stricken and suffering.
title: ‘We expected it, but now it’s here’: on the frontline of Australia’s bird flu outbreak, people are distressed

The Reserve Bank has hiked interest rates and the property market is in retreat. So far, so normal.

Donald Trump has lashed out at reports that the US is running short of key munitions in its war with Iran, threatening long prison sentences for officials who leak information about the military’s weapons stocks.

The US president claimed on Thursday that the US had “massive amounts” of ammunition and said more was being manufactured and shipped to the country, as his frustration over the conflict spilled into a public attack on the media.

title: Trump denies US running low on key munitions in war with Iran

author: Reuters in Jerusalem
description:
Yinon Levi faces trial for reckless manslaughter related to the 2025 killing of Awdah Hathaleen

Israeli prosecutors have charged a Jewish settler over the killing of a Palestinian community leader in the occupied West Bank last year- the ⁠first such indictment in nearly three years.

In papers filed by the state attorney’s office, Yinon Levi is charged with reckless manslaughter in the death of Awdah Hathaleen, a prominent ⁠activist who was involved in the 2025 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land.

Continue reading...
title: Israel charges West Bank settler over death of renowned Palestinian activist

author: Raphael Boyd
description:
Christopher Wright, 73, shot Richard Dyson in November 2019 and then dismembered his remains

A man who killed his lodger and concealed his dismembered body in a barrel filled with concrete for more than five years has been jailed for a minimum of 35 years.

Christopher Wright, a 73-year-old farmer from South Yorkshire, was convicted in July in Sheffield crown court of murdering Richard Dyson, 55, in 2019. Dyson had been living in his car on Wright’s farm in Hoyland and had been doing jobs for the then 67-year-old when the pair had a falling out.

Continue reading...
title: South Yorkshire man who killed lodger and hid body in concrete gets 35-year sentence

author: Stephen Starr in Wooster, Ohio
description:
Voters in the red district are concerned with congressman’s alleged behavior and political future ahead of the midterms

David Griffith was a registered Republican for years.

But on Sunday evening, he watched Ohio congressman Max Miller stumble through an 18-minute statement in which the lawmaker attempted to defend himself against allegations of domestic abuse against his ex-wife and infant child.

Continue reading...
title: Ohio voters reconsider Republican Max Miller amid domestic abuse allegations

author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
description:
Pia Dandiya, a first-time candidate, says voters care more about costs than district lines as she seeks a key open seat

What is a sanguine new congressional candidate to do when the district they thought they were running in gets torn apart by a governor’s best efforts to gerrymander his state at the president’s behest?

For Pia Dandiya, a first-time candidate for the Democratic party in Florida, the answer was simple: pick up some maps, hit the road, and embrace the challenge of conquering a different part of the state.

Continue reading...
title: Florida Democrat switches districts after DeSantis redistricting shake-up

author: Associated Press
description:
Fires have destroyed about 850 buildings and forced about 67,000 people to evacuate since they erupted last weekend

Firefighters have taken advantage of cooler weather to begin getting a handle on wildfires that have displaced tens of thousands of people around Washington state’s second-largest city, but hotter, drier and breezier days lie ahead.

Officials reported Wednesday that firefighters had established containment lines around the perimeters of all three fires affecting Spokane and that they were focused on reinforcing those lines. Temperatures were expected to climb from the 80sF the past two days into the upper 90sF (36C), with less humidity, late this week.

Continue reading...
title: Firefighters start to contain Washington state wildfires as tens of thousands remain displaced

author: Rajeev Syal
description:
Programme aiming to stop people turning to terrorism sees 39% rise in referrals in year to September 2025 – the highest number on record

A record number of people have been referred to the government’s anti-terror programme, with a 39% rise over the last year, including a 20% rise in referrals for extreme rightwing ideology, according to official data released on Thursday.

A total of 10,293 referrals – up from 7,408 – were made to the Prevent programme in the year to September 2025, which is the highest number since records began 11 years ago.

Continue reading...
title: Extreme rightwing referrals to Prevent rise 20% amid record anti-terror reporting

author: Gaya Gupta
description:
When asked to detail what would make a better life in three to five years, 60% of US adults said greater financial security

Americans may seem increasingly divided on beliefs and values, but in a new survey of more than 30,000 adults from across the country spanning generations and economic classes, a majority of Americans agree there’s a significant barrier to achieving a better life: the rising cost of living.

When asked to describe what a better life in three to five years would look like, 60% of Americans said they wanted greater financial security, according to a survey that was conducted by the McKinsey Institute for Economic Mobility and the WK Kellogg Foundation in mid-April.

Continue reading...
title: Most Americans view rising living costs as biggest barrier to a better life, survey finds

author: Sophie Sullivan
description:
Experts say growing trend on sites such as Polymarket and Kalshi could motivate people to start fires to win money

A group of US lawmakers is sounding the alarm over prediction market platforms that allow users to bet on wildfires, as experts warn the emerging trend could raise the risk of arson.

Democratic senators from six states sent a letter this week to the chair of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), an independent government agency regulating platforms such as Polymarket and Kalshi, urging it to rein in the practice.

Continue reading...
title: US senators urge crackdown on wildfire betting amid warnings of arson risk

author: Caroline Davies
description:
Grammy-winning pianist Robert Glasper will headline opening of club’s first UK venue in Covent Garden next month

The world-famous New York jazz club Blue Note will open its first UK venue in London next month.

Located in the basement of St Martins Lane hotel, Covent Garden, the club promises the best of British jazz alongside world-class international artists, with a programme featuring emerging and established talent.

Continue reading...
title: Blue Note to bring world-famous jazz club to London

author: Richard Adams Education editor

George Holmes was suspended in 2025 over allegations involving financial mismanagement and other misconduct

The University of Greater Manchester’s embattled vice-chancellor has had his contract terminated by the university’s governing body, ending a period of uncertainty over the university’s leadership.

Sir George Holmes, who had led the university for two decades, was initially suspended last year over allegations involving financial mismanagement and other misconduct.

Continue reading...
title: University of Greater Manchester ends contract of embattled vice-chancellor

Mark Parton, the leader of the opposition in the Australian Capital Territory, made the admission after an anonymous complaint referred to the Legislative Assembly’s commissioner for standards alleged that last week’s text was sent to a sex worker.

Meta said on Wednesday that one of its AI models hacked ⁠another company during cybersecurity testing, after an error by its testing partner gave the model unintended internet access.

The incident adds to a ⁠growing list of ⁠cases in ​which AI agents from major developers breached systems at other companies during testing, after Anthropic said last week that some of its models ⁠hacked three companies, and OpenAI disclosed that an AI agent breached the startup Hugging Face.

title: Meta says its AI model hacked into another company during testing
